code_label: Stock trend prediction is difficult
text_span: financial time series signals are characterized by non-stationary, long memory and low signal-to-noise ratio, which make it difficult to be forecasted.
rationale: States the core problem motivating the study.

code_label: Model combines frequency, external factors, and quantum circuits
text_span: a frequency-domain enhanced bi-directional recurrent quantum network (FDBRQ) is proposed in this paper, which takes into account the influence of external factors and is able to achieve multi-step prediction.
rationale: Summarizes the proposed model and its intended capabilities.

code_label: Frequency-domain embedding extracts features
text_span: a frequency-domain embedding module (FDEM) is used to extract the frequency-domain features of the price series and convert the input stock price time series data into embedding vectors.
rationale: Identifies the first major model component and its function.

code_label: External feature attention enhances representation
text_span: we introduce the external feature attention enhancement (EFAE), which utilizes external factor data to enhance the representation of the embedding vectors.
rationale: Captures the external-variable integration mechanism.

code_label: Bi-directional quantum recurrent structure captures long-term dependence
text_span: a quantum neural network with bi-directional recurrent structure is designed to capture the long-term dependence of the financial time series.
rationale: States the architectural choice used to model temporal dependence.

code_label: Experimental superiority on four Chinese stock datasets
text_span: Experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms other models on the four stock datasets from Chinese stock market.
rationale: Main empirical finding reported in the abstract.

code_label: Need for better forecasting support
text_span: Researchers are committed to finding an effective prediction model to better support investment decisions.
rationale: Frames the practical motivation for the work.

code_label: Single-model methods are not sensitive enough
text_span: these methods using a single model are not sensitive enough to abrupt changes in stock price trends.
rationale: Identifies a limitation of prior single-model approaches.

code_label: Global decomposition may leak future information
text_span: the decomposed signal will be mixed with future information, which leads to the features of the future signal being leaked to the learner in advance
rationale: States a methodological caveat about prior multiscale approaches.

code_label: Long-term multistep prediction underexplored
text_span: long-term multistep prediction, as a challenging task, has not received sufficient attention and research to date.
rationale: Defines a research gap the paper aims to address.

code_label: Causal frequency-domain learning avoids future information
text_span: the historical time series are fed into the frequency-domain embedding module to learn to extract the frequency-domain features of the signals without using future information, which is consistent with practical applications.
rationale: Explains a causal design decision in the proposed pipeline.

code_label: Bi-directional quantum circuits process forward and reverse order
text_span: consisting of two quantum circuits, one propagating temporal features in time order, and the other propagating temporal features in reverse order.
rationale: Describes the bi-directional recurrent quantum design.

code_label: Quantum computation and neural networks enhance capability
text_span: The quantum neural network integrates the parallelism of quantum computation and the advantages of neural networks
rationale: States the claimed benefit of combining quantum and neural approaches.

code_label: External factors are important in stock markets
text_span: since the stock market is highly correlated with external factors, we also introduce external feature attention enhancement
rationale: Motivates inclusion of exogenous variables.

code_label: FDEM uses VMD and normalization layers
text_span: including variational mode decomposition (VMD), layer normalization (LN), batch normalization (BN), full dimension convolution, channel average pooling, and fully connected layers.
rationale: Lists the main operations in the embedding module.

code_label: VMD decomposes signal into IMFs
text_span: the VMD constructs the variational problem model.
rationale: Introduces the decomposition method used in FDEM.

code_label: Layer normalization and batch normalization are combined
text_span: we incorporate two normalization techniques, layer normalization and batch normalization sequentially.
rationale: Records a specific architectural choice for stabilization and training.

code_label: Normalization combination improves performance and generalization
text_span: Combining their advantages can improve the performance and generalization ability of neural networks.
rationale: States the intended benefit of the normalization design.

code_label: Full-dimension convolution extracts correlations
text_span: Convolution kernels of different sizes are used in order to fully extract the correlation between features.
rationale: Explains why multiple kernel sizes are used.

code_label: Channel averaging compresses feature maps
text_span: we perform channel averaging pooling on the feature map.
rationale: Captures the dimensionality-reduction step in FDEM.

code_label: QCU has encoder and ansatz
text_span: a QCU consists of two parts, Encode and Ansatz.
rationale: Defines the quantum circuit unit structure.

code_label: Quantum encoder converts classical data to quantum data
text_span: The Quantum Encoder is used to convert the input classical data into quantum data.
rationale: States the role of the encoder component.

code_label: Quantum ansatz is trainable
text_span: The Quantum Ansatz is used to process the input quantum signal and prepare the corresponding quantum state, which is also the part that needs to be optimized during the training.
rationale: Identifies the trainable part of the quantum circuit.

code_label: Quantum gates implement the circuit
text_span: The basic quantum gates used in QCU and their corresponding matrix representations and quantum circuit diagrams are shown in Table 1.
rationale: Shows the gate-based implementation of the model.

code_label: External attention vector is generated from factors
text_span: By passing through the fully connected layer and softmax layer, an external attention vector At is generated at the t-th time step.
rationale: Describes how exogenous variables are transformed into attention weights.

code_label: Attention-enhanced embedding is formed by elementwise operations
text_span: The enhanced embedding vector Et’ is obtained by weighting the attention vector At on the embedding vector Et at the current time step via elementwise multiplication and addition.
rationale: Specifies the fusion operation used in EFAE.

code_label: Data source is JoinQuant and four CSI 300 stocks
text_span: The data source used in this paper is the JoinQuant platform
rationale: Identifies the empirical data source.

code_label: Three prediction horizons are tested
text_span: we use historical data to forecast the stock closing prices for the next 1, 5 and 20 trading days, respectively.
rationale: States the experimental forecasting horizons.

code_label: Log differencing and Min-Max standardization are applied
text_span: we first smoothed the original series by logarithmic differencing
rationale: Describes the preprocessing applied to the target series.

code_label: External factors are cleaned with forward fill, MAD, and scaling
text_span: we employ forward filling to maintain data continuity
rationale: Summarizes the preprocessing pipeline for exogenous variables.

code_label: Huber-like loss is used
text_span: the loss function we use to minimize is as follows
rationale: Identifies the training objective used for optimization.

code_label: Loss gradient is stable for small and large errors
text_span: when the difference y −̂y is small, the gradient value is small enough to make the model parameters stable; when the difference y −̂y is large, the gradient value is not so large as to destroy the model parameters.
rationale: Explains why the chosen loss is numerically stable.

code_label: RMSE, MAE, and MAPE are evaluation metrics
text_span: we use three evaluation metrics, namely, the root mean square error (RMSE), the mean absolute error (MAE) and the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE).
rationale: States the metrics used to compare models.

code_label: Factor screening uses IC and IR
text_span: we use information coefficient (IC) and information ratio (IR) as evaluation criteria.
rationale: Describes the factor-selection criteria.

code_label: Top three factors per category are selected
text_span: we select the top 3 factors with the highest absolute values of IR as partial input variables for the model.
rationale: Specifies the selection rule for external factors.

code_label: ACF and PACF guide input length
text_span: We determine it with the help of plots of the autocorrelation function (ACF) and the partial autocorrelation function (PACF)
rationale: Explains how the input window length is chosen.

code_label: Input length is 20 for one-step prediction
text_span: we set T = 20
rationale: Records the chosen window size for short-term prediction.

code_label: Input length increases for multistep prediction
text_span: we set T as 48 for the 5-step prediction model and 96 for the 20-step prediction model.
rationale: Records the chosen window sizes for longer horizons.

code_label: VMD over-decomposition avoided at K=7
text_span: When K ≥ 8, there are modes with similar center frequencies, which can be considered as over-decomposition. Therefore, we set K = 7.
rationale: Explains the selected number of decompositions.

code_label: Quantum system size limited to six qubits
text_span: we choose quantum systems with n = 6 qubits.
rationale: States a practical constraint on quantum model size.

code_label: FDBRQ achieves best one-step performance
rationale: Indicates the best reported 1-step metrics among compared methods.

code_label: External factors reduce prediction errors
text_span: When considering the incorporation of external factors into the model for prediction, the prediction errors decrease significantly.
rationale: Reports the observed benefit of exogenous variables.

code_label: LSTM may overfit on some datasets
text_span: the LSTM method with simple structure may suffer from the problem of overfitting
rationale: Notes a dataset-dependent weakness of a baseline model.

code_label: Deep LSTM outperforms bi-directional LSTM in one-step task
text_span: the deep LSTM structure performs better than the bi-directional LSTM structure
rationale: Reports a comparative finding among recurrent baselines.

code_label: Rolling prediction accumulates errors
text_span: the prediction errors will gradually accumulate and be revealed during the iterations of rolling prediction.
rationale: Explains why iterative forecasting performs poorly.

code_label: Multistep prediction avoids cumulative error
text_span: multistep prediction does not rely on previous prediction results, and directly outputs the forecast for multiple future time steps
rationale: Contrasts the neural approach with rolling prediction.

code_label: FDBRQ performs best in 5-step prediction
text_span: our proposed method performs the best and exhibits relatively stable results in the 5-step prediction task
rationale: Summarizes the main medium-term empirical result.

code_label: Rolling methods have large errors in 20-step prediction
text_span: the rolling prediction methods have large errors.
rationale: Reports poor long-horizon performance of classical rolling methods.

code_label: Bi-directional LSTM is advantageous for long sequences
text_span: the bi-directional LSTM can better capture the features of long-term memory.
rationale: States a comparative observation for long-horizon forecasting.

code_label: FDBRQ remains stable and most accurate in 20-step prediction
text_span: our proposed method still maintains a stable prediction performance and shows the best accuracy.
rationale: Reports the main long-term empirical finding.

code_label: Model is closest to real values in visual comparisons
text_span: the prediction results of our proposed method are closest to the real values.
rationale: Summarizes the visual assessment of the forecasts.

code_label: Quantum models are slower on classical computers
text_span: when attempting to construct quantum neural networks with more qubits, the training speed on traditional classic computers tends to be relatively slow.
rationale: States a practical implementation limitation.

code_label: Future work targets better quantum design and speed
text_span: future research will focus on the design of quantum neural networks to better handle the time–frequency domain features of financial time series and improve the robustness and running speed of the models.
rationale: Identifies the authors' stated future direction.
